genres.lead: Sunny jazz chords on a dusty Rhodes, a flute on the tune and a beat that never hurries. Every seed gives a new warm lofi tune, written in your browser, and you can change every part of the track.
sound: Warm is the sunniest of Lolly's three Lofi moods, always in a major key. A Rhodes, a Wurlitzer, a soft pluck or a felt piano plays major and minor ninths voiced close, each chord moving as little as possible from the last. A flute most often carries the tune, or vibes, a kalimba or an acoustic guitar, and some tunes have no lead at all, just the keys.

The beat is mostly a swung boom-bap played a little behind the grid, with a shuffle, a lazy groove, half-time or a sparse kick in other tunes, over a rolling, upright or synth bass. Tunes play at about 75 to 99 beats a minute, through a worn record's tiny ticks of dust, an occasional pop and the soft noise of the stylus.

Each tune opens its own way (the keys alone, the hats and then the kit, or the bass and hats) and plays a verse that the melody joins halfway. Two or three middle sections follow: a bridge, a feature for the lead, the keys or a walking bass, a groove with the beat held back, a breakdown or a drum break. A last verse leads to a fade.
uses: Podcast intros and beds under talk

A felt piano or a Rhodes (now and then a Wurlitzer or a soft pluck) plays minor ninths and elevenths, voiced close and moving as little as possible from chord to chord. Many tunes have no lead at all; the rest bring in vibes, a flute, a harp or a kalimba.

The drums stay soft: a rimshot or brushes more often than a snare, a half-time or lazy groove, and sometimes a sparse kick with no hats at all. A rolling or upright bass holds the root. Tunes play at about 63 to 86 beats a minute, with a worn record's dust and the stylus's soft noise underneath.

A tune can open on the keys alone or on the hats, then plays a verse that the melody joins halfway. Two or three middle sections follow, such as a bridge on the second progression, a groove with the beat held back or a breakdown with no drums, before a last verse and an ending that fades or thins out.

The lead stays quiet and sparse, a vocal chop, bells, vibes or a flute half-buried in the dust, and comes in only halfway through the first drop. Tunes play at about 116 to 124 beats a minute.

A tune opens on a long, filtered intro (the chords, the beat or the bass alone), then a verse and a build. The full kick arrives at the drop, where the filter closes and opens again over eight or sixteen bars, and the breakdown is the chords and the bass alone before the next build.
